headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: xonsh can read/write and egress broadly, while Superset exposes API-driven analytics workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Superset has no documented shared channel to xonsh, but xonsh can read files and run shell commands, so manual copy-paste or file handoff could carry malicious instructions into shell execution. The pathway is not default or automatic, so this stays low.
conditions: IF an operator copies Superset output into xonsh stdin/stdout or a file consumed by xonsh
IF Superset content is treated as shell instructions in xonsh
mitigations: Use a strict copy/paste boundary and never execute pasted text directly
Prefix any transferred text with a non-executable delimiter
Review transferred content before running it in xonsh
Keep Superset outputs in read-only exports
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: xonsh can read filesystem contents and has broad network egress, while Superset can call APIs and is documented as a data-engineering tool. If they share a workspace, xonsh can expose files or environment data that Superset workflows may surface or transmit. The shared-data pathway is plausible in default use, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or exported files
IF xonsh reads secrets or configuration from the filesystem and those artifacts are later surfaced by Superset
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Remove secrets from shared directories
Restrict xonsh to a minimal read-only mount
Audit Superset exports before sharing
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Superset can call APIs, and xonsh can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses. Even without git writes, overlapping access to shared files or API-backed resources can cause clobbering or inconsistent state. The conflict is plausible in default multi-tool workflows, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or generated artifact set
IF an API-backed workflow in Superset and a shell workflow in xonsh target the same mutable resource
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Make one agent read-only
Check for file existence before overwrite
requires-engineering: add resource locking in the orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: Superset can produce analytics outputs that xonsh may consume as shell inputs or scripts, and xonsh can execute those results without built-in verification. That creates a realistic chain where one agent's output becomes the other's action trigger, with moderate blast radius.
conditions: IF Superset output is piped into xonsh without validation
IF xonsh executes commands derived from Superset-generated text
mitigations: Insert a human review step before execution
Validate outputs against an allowlist
Use structured data formats instead of free text
Log and diff generated commands
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and show no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch. The only documented compliance-relevant surface is xonsh's filesystem and environment-variable access, but Superset has no stated sensitive-data handling. With no concrete mismatch, risk is low rather than none because the profiles are sparse.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the shared filesystem
IF an operator relies on undocumented retention or residency behavior
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared paths
Document retention expectations
Limit environment-variable exposure
Review logs for sensitive fields
requires-engineering: map data residency and retention controls
